messages.author: d7fd273d0b8c973d
messages.subject: Error in names (results1) <- geog.info$ranges ?
parts:
Hello.

I managed to fix the RAM problem and got the run to work. 

However, after the run is finished, I am having this error, and I think it might be related to saving the results as a table:

Read 12 items

Read 720 items

Error in names(results1) <- geog.info$ranges : 

  'names' attribute [1024] must be the same length as the vector [638]

Calls: get.biogeobears.results.by.range.table

Execution halted


This is my script:

#####

setwd("~/R/BGB/all_t/dec_j/")
library(BioGeoBEARS)
library(optimx)
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/cladoRcpp.R") # (needed now that traits model added; source FIRST!)
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_add_fossils_randomly_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_basics_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_calc_transition_matrices_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_classes_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_detection_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_DNA_cladogenesis_sim_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_extract_Qmat_COOmat_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_generics_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_models_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_on_multiple_trees_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_plots_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_readwrite_v1.R")

source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_SSEsim_makePlots_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_SSEsim_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_stochastic_mapping_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_stratified_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_univ_model_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/calc_uppass_probs_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/calc_loglike_sp_v01.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/get_stratified_subbranch_top_downpass_likelihoods_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/runBSM_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/stochastic_map_given_inputs.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/summarize_BSM_tables_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_traits_v1.R") # added traits model
calc_loglike_sp = compiler::cmpfun(calc_loglike_sp_prebyte)    # crucial to fix bug in uppass calculations
calc_independent_likelihoods_on_each_branch = compiler::cmpfun(calc_independent_likelihoods_on_each_branch_prebyte)
require(parallel)

decj.potamo <- define_BioGeoBEARS_run()

phylo.path <- "data/potamo_d6.newick" 
moref(phylo.path)
potamo.tree <- read.tree(phylo.path)

prt(potamo.tree, get_tipnames = T)

decj.potamo$trfn = "data/potamo_d6.newick"
decj.potamo$trfn

geo.path <- "data/potamo_code_geog.data" 
moref(geo.path)
getranges_from_LagrangePHYLIP(lgdata_fn=geo.path) #infer ranges from phylip file

decj.potamo$geogfn = "data/potamo_code_geog.data"
decj.potamo$geogfn 

decj.potamo = configure.standard.biogeobears.run(decj.potamo)

decj.potamo$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["j","type"] = "free"
decj.potamo$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["j","init"] = 0.0001
decj.potamo$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["j","est"] = 0.0001
decj.potamo$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["j","min"] = 0.0001

decj.potamo$max_range_size = 5
decj.potamo$include_null_range = TRUE

decj.potamo$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table

decj.potamo$use_optimx = TRUE
decj.potamo$num_cores_to_use = 10

decj.potamo$return_condlikes_table = T
decj.potamo$calc_TTL_loglike_from_condlikes_table = T
decj.potamo$calc_ancprobs = T

check_BioGeoBEARS_run(decj.potamo)
decj.potamo

decj.results = bears_optim_run(decj.potamo)
save(decj.results, file="results/decj.potamo.Rdata") 


decj.range.table = get.biogeobears.results.by.range.table(decj.results)

write.table(dec.range.table, "results/decj.potamo.ranges.tsv", sep = "\t", row.names = F)

decj.area.table = get.biogeobears.results.by.range.table(decj.results)

write.table(dec.area.table, "results/decj.potamo.areas.tsv", sep = "\t", row.names = F)

# Save analysis plot in pdf/SVG
# Ranges
svg("potamo_decj_ranges_plot.svg")
plot.biogeobears.results.ranges(results.object = decj.results, analysis.title = "DEC+J")
dev.off()
pdf("potamo_decj_ranges_plot.pdf")
plot.biogeobears.results.ranges(results.object = decj.results, analysis.title = "DEC+J")
dev.off()

#Areas
svg("potamo_decj_areas_plot.svg")
plot.biogeobears.results.areas(results.object = decj.results, analysis.title = "DEC+J")
dev.off()
pdf("potamo_decj_areas_plot.pdf")
plot.biogeobears.results.areas(results.object = decj.results, analysis.title = "DEC+J")
dev.off()

#####

I can attach the tree and geography files if needed.

Any ideas of what might be going on?

Cheers

JP

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Error in names (results1) <- geog.info$ranges ?
parts:
Hi -- it looks like "get.biogeobears.results.by.range.table" is a function Jeet made for a tutorial he gave in 2015:
https://www.google.com/search?q=%22get.biogeobears.results.by.range.table%22&cad=h

...it's not part of the official BioGeoBEARS code. 

I'm carrying a baby around so I can't diagnose it, but based on your code it looks like you could just comment those lines out and everything else would work. In general I would recommend using The Official Example Script as your template for analysis:

http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#script

If your goal was to get a nice table of the range probabilities for each node, see:

Table of probabilities of states/ranges at each node
http://phylo.wikidot.com/example-biogeobears-scripts#node_probabilities


Cheers,
Nick
